mainEntity.name: How accurate is a BAC calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: It gives a rough, population-average estimate. Two people drinking the same amount can have very different BACs because of food, drinking speed, body composition, medications and metabolism. Only a breath or blood test measures BAC.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for BAC to reach zero?

acceptedAnswer.text: The body removes alcohol at a commonly estimated rate of about 0.015% per hour (a conservative figure; measured rates vary widely between people, roughly 0.009–0.035% per hour), and nothing — coffee, cold showers or exercise — speeds this up. A BAC of 0.08% takes about 5 hours or more to clear.

mainEntity.name: What counts as a standard drink?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the US, a standard drink contains about 14 grams (0.6 fl oz) of pure alcohol — roughly a 12-oz beer at 5%, a 5-oz glass of wine at 12%, or a 1.5-oz shot of 40% spirits. Craft beers, large pours and cocktails often contain more.

mainEntity.name: How many drinks does it take to reach 0.08% BAC?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on weight and sex. For a 160 lb man the peak estimate reaches 0.08% at about 2.8 standard drinks, and for a 160 lb woman at about 2.3. Drinking slowly lowers the real figure, but impairment starts earlier.
BAC = alcohol in grams divided by (body weight in grams times r), times 100, minus elimination over time. R is 0.68 for men and 0.55 for women, and elimination is estimated at 0.015% per hour.

mainEntity.name: Why is the estimate higher for women at the same weight?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Widmark factor r is lower for women (0.55 against 0.68), which reflects a lower average share of body water, so the same alcohol gives a higher concentration.

mainEntity.name: What is the legal BAC limit in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: 0.08% for drivers 21 and over in every state except Utah, which uses 0.05%. Commercial drivers are limited to 0.04% and drivers under 21 face zero tolerance laws.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a BAC calculator to decide if I can drive?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is an educational estimate, and impairment begins below the legal limits. If you have been drinking, use a taxi, rideshare, public transport or a sober driver.
